I wrote the 30-minute lesson on O3 at `lessons/0001-context-and-memory.html`. I haven't opened it in a browser. Quiz 0002 and its key are ready.

**What the lesson covers:** By the end, you can decide whether a piece of information in the makerspace assistant belongs in the context window, in a saved note, or in a searchable manual.
- **Context window:** what's in it on each call, and why the program re-sends it every time.
- **Between steps:** history only grows, and a worked token tally shows you pay for the sum of all calls, not the peak. It also covers context rot.
- **Between sessions:** a new session starts empty, so anything remembered has to be saved outside the model.
- **Retrieval:** loading only the relevant manual pages, up front or just in time.
- **Notes:** a per-student record, plus compaction and clearing old tool results.
- **Practice:** a four-question decision rule, a worked sort of four items, and a faded sort for you to try.

It has three figures, inline practice checks, and a warm-up that revisits the agent loop.

**Sources:** The main source is Anthropic's "Effective context engineering for AI agents". The lesson also cites the Claude context-window docs and "Building effective agents", and all three are in `RESOURCES.md`. I read the context-engineering post in full and only saw search snippets of the other two. The token counts in the worked example are made up for illustration, and the lesson says so.

**Quiz 0002:** It has five items (two multiple choice, one numeric, two short answer) on the same objective, and none repeat the lesson's practice questions. I introduced misconception ids M7 to M9 for the wrong options and recorded them in `NOTES.md`. I haven't graded or recorded anything about your understanding yet.

I didn't write a cheat sheet this time.

Ask me anything about the lesson, or tell me when you want to take the quiz.
